text: Hi, Professor. I was hoping I could talk to you about something that came up in your lecture. Of course, what can I help you with? I wanted to ask you about the concept of biocultural anthropology. I’m not sure I fully understand it. Well, biocultural anthropology is the study of how culture and biology interact with each other. For example, we might study how a certain culture uses plants for medicine. So, it’s basically the study of how culture and biology affect each other? Exactly. We’re interested in how biology affects culture and how culture affects biology. And what are some of the methods that biocultural anthropologists use to study these interactions? Well, we might use things like ethnography or fieldwork to observe and collect data about a certain group of people. We might also use things like DNA analysis or medical records to look at the biological side of things. That makes sense. Thank you for taking the time to explain that to me!
